correctness.rationale: For all n>=2 the constructed graph has diameter two; forbidden geodesic triples are exactly induced P3 subgraphs. The root/selected-original/selected-twin classification in the proof has both necessity and sufficiency; its enumerators simplify to the stated polynomial. The exact coefficients are checked algebraically. For k>=5 the coefficients are products of binomial coefficients and positive strictly concave quadratic weights, so are strictly log-concave. Exact displayed polynomial differences establish k=1,2,3,4, including boundaries n=2 and n=3. The packaged Python verifier independently enumerates 174752 initial subsets using BFS distances and checks n=2..250 arithmetic; these tests supplement an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest close prior, Thomas et al. (arXiv:2203.08170, Section 3 and Corollary 2), gives general MGP-partition descriptions and the extremal number n+1, with unique maximum set for n>=3, but not the complete cardinality polynomial or its strict log-concavity. Iršič et al. (arXiv:2401.05696, Sections 3-4) study general-position polynomials of other families. Roy et al. (arXiv:2403.05120, Sections 4-5) address numerical visibility and general-position parameters under graph operations. The new theorem is the explicit all-size count jointly with an all-n strict coefficient inequality; the known maximum is explicitly excluded from novelty.

The literature assessment is neither an independent originality certification nor a guarantee of global novelty.

value.rationale: The Mycielskian is a standard graph operation central to chromatic graph theory, and general-position polynomials form a motivated modern counting problem. The theorem gives all coefficients for an infinite classical family and proves strict log-concavity, a qualitative regularity result stronger than mere unimodality. This is not a fixed-size table, a relabeling of a known scalar maximum, or an unsupported proposed application. Scope is one construction on complete graphs; no larger theorem is claimed.
